A1.justification: Both PDFs describe WeSCon and provide readable text, equations, figures, tables and appendices. Existing material can be matched despite appendix renumbering and relocation of the checklist.

before.justification: v1 reports original synthesis experiments, listener evaluations, component ablations, training analyses and out-of-domain results, including Tables 1–5.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds an experiment on speaking-rate variation and emotion similarity in Appendix C, Table 5.

M1.justification: The CosyVoice2-based teacher/student framework, transition smoothing, prompt-token resampling, dynamic emotional attention bias and training objectives are unchanged. New Appendix C evaluates the existing mechanism.

E1.justification: Both retain LibriSpeech-100-Clean, AISHELL-1, ESD-based English/Chinese synthesis, SEED test-zh and CASIA evaluation. The added analysis samples existing test utterances within an already studied resampling range, without adding dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: Index-TTS, F5-TTS, Spark-TTS and CosyVoice2 remain the comparators in the corresponding multilingual and CASIA experiments. CosyVoice2 remains the standard zero-shot comparator; the new sensitivity study introduces no comparison method.

E3.justification: New Appendix C specifies 100 randomly selected test prompts, fixed target text across conditions and resampling ratios from 0.5 to 2.0 in 0.25 increments. It compares Emo2v scores against original and rate-matched references. Existing training and evaluation protocols are retained.

E4.justification: v1 already studies output speed and removal of speed control. v2 adds a focused sensitivity analysis testing how resampling and reference-rate matching affect emotion similarity. Existing ablations, generalization tests and training analyses remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Both report MOS means and 95% confidence intervals based on 15 listeners using the same procedure. New Table 5 provides point estimates without adding repeated-run, seed or uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: New Table 5 adds seven conditions: original-reference/rate-matched Emo2v scores are 0.57/0.86 at ratio 0.5, 0.90/0.90 at 1.0 and 0.51/0.87 at 2.0. Tables 1–4 and the CASIA results, renumbered from Table 5 to Table 6, retain their values.

T1.justification: The attention-bias formulation, training objectives in Equations (1)–(5) and attention-template definitions are retained. The new rate–emotion analysis adds no mathematical definition, derivation or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims about self-training for word-level emotion and speed control without transition-containing training data, state-of-the-art performance and preservation of zero-shot capabilities.

C2.justification: Appendix C newly discusses coupling between speed and emotion, reference-rate dependence and reduced emotional consistency outside a suggested natural resampling range of approximately 0.75–1.5. It proposes spectral and pitch distortion as an explanation. Existing Section 5 limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: The displayed sample-access link changes from an anonymous demo to the named WeSCon page. Appendix G.1 drops v1 Appendix F.1's explicit 16-bit audio-storage detail without reporting a replacement format. Existing hardware, hyperparameters and filtering specifications are retained.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion and all 68 reference entries are unchanged. The revision introduces no additional cited work or substantive change in novelty positioning.

P1.justification: v2 inserts Appendix C and a corresponding main-text pointer, moves the checklist before the technical appendices, updates affiliations and the conference footer, and adds acknowledgements. Most existing scientific prose remains verbatim.

P2.justification: v2 adds Table 5, reduces Figure 7's displayed size and reflows existing material. The retained prompt example now occupies one page, but its proper caption is replaced by raw formatting options and its reference becomes 'Listing ??'.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1's speed-control ablation and rate-versus-speed plot, Appendix C/Table 5 directly examines how rate matching affects emotion similarity, modestly improving interpretation of the evaluation. This analytical benefit outweighs the localized prompt-listing errors and removed bit-depth detail; the core method and benchmark evidence remain unchanged.
